newsitem.title: USA: U.S. repatriates three Cuban rafters.
newsitem.headline: U.S. repatriates three Cuban rafters.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard on Monday repatriated three Cubans who were picked up in the Florida Strait fleeing the communist-ruled island on a raft.
A fourth was taken to the U.S. military base at Guantanamo, southeast Cuba, where his appeal for political asylum will be assessed, a Coast Guard spokesman said.
The four were rescued by a Coast Guard cutter on Friday nine miles (14 km) east of Alligator Reef in the Florida Keys.

The Coast Guard said the fourth Cuban was taken to Guantanamo on the advise of the U.S. Immigration Service. Rafters picked up at sea customarily are questioned by INS inspectors as to whether they have a legitimate fear of political persecution should they be sent back to Cuba.

Following a crisis in September 1994 when more than 30,000 Cubans tried to cross the straits to the United States, Washington announced in May 1995 it would repatriate Cubans picked up at sea. The move ended a policy of virtual automatic asylum in the United States.
